clue.text: Scotsman, doctor, describing his masculinity

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw around it, so the outer words wrap around the inner one

parts.note: Mac is a stock name for a Scotsman
taken as written
MO is Medical Officer, a military doctor

explanation.surface: A Scottish doctor is portrayed as a strutting, macho figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' looks like part of the definition, but it is wordplay; 'describing' means drawing a line around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Machismo is an exaggerated show of male toughness, a direct synonym for aggressive masculinity.

clue.text: Novel, second by detective

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
taken as written
dick is old slang for a detective

explanation.surface: A crime novel coming in second place behind a detective story.
explanation.definitionFit: Moby-Dick is Herman Melville's whaling novel, so it is an example of a novel.

clue.text: Waterway crossing state from cape in Florida

indicators.note: a waterway crossing something spans it from side to side, so its letters lie either side of the other word

parts.note: a canal is an artificial waterway
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: A canal crosses a US state on its way from a Florida headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' suggests a US state beside Florida, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Canaveral is the headland on Florida's Atlantic coast known for its rocket launch site.

clue.text: Mole in team close to dictator

parts.note: taken as written
a side is a sports team

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of dictator

explanation.surface: A spy has infiltrated the inner circle of a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to dictator' reads as being near the tyrant, but it takes just the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a spy working from within an organisation, which is what an insider with secret access is.

clue.text: Tom, Dick, or Harry entertains them, juggling

indicators.note: a juggler keeps things tossing in the air, so these letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: the fourteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A street performer named Tom, Dick or Harry keeps a crowd amused with his juggling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom, Dick or Harry' is the idiom for any ordinary person.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'any Tom, Dick or Harry' means an ordinary person, the typical member of the public.

clue.text: Affected, American college grounds

parts.note: camp means exaggerated or affected in manner
US for the United States, American

explanation.surface: A description of the grounds of a pretentious American college.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the site and buildings of a university or college.

clue.text: Bony, a maltreated langur

indicators.note: something maltreated is knocked about, so these letters are roughed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to join the rearranged letters
a langur is an Asian monkey

explanation.surface: A mistreated monkey has become skinny.
explanation.definitionFit: Angular describes a lean frame with sharp corners, so a bony face or body is called angular.

clue.text: Finished last of frittata, Italian food

parts.note: past means over, finished

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter only

parts.note: the final letter of frittata

explanation.surface: Someone has eaten the last of the frittata, an Italian dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian food' seems to describe the frittata, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is the staple Italian food of dough shaped into noodles and other forms.

clue.text: Bandage top half of head after whack

indicators.note: after says which piece follows which when the parts are joined

parts.note: to swat is to strike, whack

indicators.note: in a down clue the top half of a word is its first half, so only its opening letters are kept

parts.note: the first two of the four letters of head

explanation.surface: Bandage the top of someone's head after they've been hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is first aid; the clue's 'Bandage' is a verb, and to swathe is to wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe is to wrap in layers of cloth, which is what bandaging a wound involves.

clue.text: Taken unawares before the dance became popular

indicators.note: before says the later words come first when the parts are joined

parts.note: a trend that catches on becomes popular
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Something about a dance craze that arrived before it caught on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' asks for the second phrase to be written first.
explanation.definitionFit: To be caught on the hop is a British idiom for being caught off guard or unprepared.

clue.text: Blessing given by one disciple on mountain

parts.note: ben is Scottish for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
I is the Roman numeral one
son can mean a disciple or follower of a teacher

explanation.surface: A blessing is bestowed by one of the disciples on a mountain, as in the Sermon on the Mount.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'one disciple on mountain' puts the first two pieces after the mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Benison is an old literary word for a blessing or benediction.

clue.text: Imposing, a state capital

parts.note: august means dignified and imposing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of an impressive state capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' seems to belong to the definition, but it supplies the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta is the capital city of the US state of Maine.

clue.text: Excited holding data about earnest biblical combatants

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jumbled letters surround the remaining word
excited things are stirred up, so these letters are agitated into a new order

parts.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged
avid means keen, eager, earnest

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to be holding data about something earnest, perhaps a researcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' looks like the container signal, but it is part of the letters to be jumbled; 'about' does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: David and Goliath are the shepherd boy and Philistine giant who fought in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Profession out East for one into social welfare?

indicators.note: out means removed, so this letter is taken away

parts.note: a career is a profession
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Someone whose profession, out in the East, is social welfare work.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the two Es is dropped from the profession word. The question mark flags a loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A carer looks after people who need help, so is someone devoted to the welfare of others.

clue.text: Bit of magic involving a bowler?

definitions.text: Bit of magic involving a bowler?

parts.words: Bit of magic involving a bowler?
parts.note: surface reading: a conjuror's trick with a bowler hat, such as pulling out a rabbit

parts.words: Bit of magic involving a bowler?
parts.note: setter's reading: a cricket bowler's feat of taking three wickets with consecutive balls

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler throws the ball at the batsman; taking three wickets in successive balls is a famous feat, and a conjuror pulls tricks from a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricketing feat of three wickets in a row is magical bowling, and a conjuror's trick with headgear fits too.

clue.text: Curry favour with eccentric queen, perhaps

parts.note: to court someone is to seek their favour
a card is an eccentric or amusing person

explanation.surface: Someone sucks up to an eccentric queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queen' suggests royalty, but it is the playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: A court card is a king, queen or jack in a pack of playing cards, so a queen is one example.

clue.text: Senator confused by instrument

indicators.note: something confused is muddled up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged
by as in multiplication, three by four, is the times sign X

explanation.surface: A politician is baffled by a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a link word, but it is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor sax is a saxophone pitched between the alto and baritone, a wind instrument.

clue.text: Vaudeville star left judge in bawdy saloon

indicators.note: in says the earlier pieces sit inside the jumbled word
bawdy means rowdy and coarse, so the letters of the following word are disorderly

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
the six letters to be rearranged
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A vaudeville star walked out on a judge in a rowdy bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' reads as walked out, but it gives a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Jolson was an American entertainer who became a star of vaudeville and then of the first talking picture.

clue.text: The M25, say — what's said about small section?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the spoken word goes round the small piece

parts.note: oral means spoken, said rather than written
a bit is a small piece

explanation.surface: A question about the M25 motorway and what is said of one small stretch of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The M25 is the motorway that rings London. 'what's said' hints at a homophone, but it is the word for spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbital road is a ring road circling a city, and the M25 is London's orbital motorway.

clue.text: A clipped English accent

parts.note: taken as written
clipped means cut
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A description of a crisp, clipped English way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accent' suggests a manner of speech; it is the written mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute is the accent mark sloping upward over a vowel, as in café.

clue.text: Sailor only gets shellfish

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman, a sailor
alone means only, solely

explanation.surface: A sailor manages to catch nothing but shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: The abalone is an edible sea snail with an ear-shaped shell, a kind of shellfish.

clue.text: Margin of safety in course of action supporting Confederate general

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits underneath, so it is written after the other

parts.note: Robert E. Lee led the Confederate army in the American Civil War
a way is a method, a course of action

explanation.surface: A cautious military plan backing up a Civil War general.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is room to manoeuvre, an allowance that gives a safety margin.

clue.text: A military display? Darn — it ought to be abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so these letters run loose into a new order

parts.note: the fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling that a military display ought to be scrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' reads as cancelled, but it means unrestrained.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edinburgh Military Tattoo is an annual display of massed bands at Edinburgh Castle; a tattoo is such a military show.

clue.text: Tailless wading bird, unknown on a Balearic island

indicators.note: without a tail, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the ibis is a long-billed wading bird
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns
taken as written

explanation.surface: A curious bird with no tail, unrecorded on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is one of the Balearic Islands, the Spanish group in the western Mediterranean.

clue.text: Artist has no reason, at first, to sound surprised

indicators.note: having none of something means it is taken away

parts.note: James McNeill Whistler was an American painter

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of reason

explanation.surface: A painter with no rational explanation expresses astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A low whistle is a common way of showing amazement, so to whistle is to make that surprised noise.

clue.text: Pirate captain has unusual pipes

parts.note: Captain Hook is the pirate in Peter Pan

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so these letters fall out of their usual order

parts.note: the three letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Captain Hook smokes some odd pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' looks like a link word, but its letters are jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: A hookah is an oriental tobacco pipe that draws smoke through water.

clue.text: End of May, too soon for annual

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter only

parts.note: the final letter of May
early means before the expected time

explanation.surface: Late May is too early for a yearly event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' reads as the month, but only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Annual and yearly are synonyms: happening once every year.

clue.text: Something added or removed?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: supplementary material added at the end of a book

definitions.note: the clue implies 'something removed', a noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the small organ of the gut that surgeons often take out

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings look like opposites, which is the joke: one is added to a book, the other taken out of a body.
explanation.definitionFit: A book's supplement at the back and the vestigial organ removed in an appendectomy share the one name.
